advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting an OSError at record()'s open/write (real boundary) that asserts record() returns without raising (and logs a warning).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:48-52: `try: with open(path, "a", ...) as handle: handle.write(...) except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - telemetry must not fail a run` — the swallow branch is explicitly marked no-cover.

usage_log.py docstring: 'Best-effort: a telemetry sink must never break the LLM call path, so any write error is logged and swallowed rather than raised into the runner.' — a stated contract with no corresponding test.

ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_usage_log.py has no test that makes open()/write() raise OSError (e.g. monkeypatching the actual open at the seam, or pointing REBAR_USAGE_LOG at an unwritable path) and asserts record() does not propagate.
advisory.finding: The best-effort error-swallow contract in record() — 'a telemetry sink must never break the LLM call path, so any write error is logged and swallowed rather than raised into the runner' — is untested. No test injects an OSError at open()/write() to assert record() returns without raising. If a future refactor let the error propagate, the LLM call path in the billable CI jobs would break and the suite would not catch the regression.
scenarios: A refactor changes the except clause or narrows the caught exception type, letting a write failure propagate into PydanticAIRunner.run during a weekly billable job.
